Get your laptop ready before Day 1. Plan **30–60 minutes** the day before — not the morning of. The optional [Day 0](Schedule.qmd#day-0-optional-software-setup-computational-refresher) session is the place to bring any install errors you can't solve yourself.

::: callout-tip
**What you'll have at the end:**

1. R, RStudio, Git, and a working terminal
2. Every R / Bioconductor package the workshop uses
3. The workshop datasets installed (`ifnb`, `stxBrain`) or downloaded (NSCLC, scATAC PBMC 10k)
4. A clean `sessionInfo()` confirming the environment
:::

## 1. Required tools

- **R ≥ 4.4** — [download](https://www.r-project.org)
- **RStudio Desktop** (current release) — [download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
- **Git ≥ 2.30** — [download](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
- **A GitHub account** — [sign up](https://github.com/signup)
- **A terminal that supports `ssh`** (only required for the Talapas Advanced bonus track)
- *(Optional, but recommended)* **VS Code** for editing files on Talapas via SSH — see the [VS Code & Talapas](Resources_Folder/VSCode_Talapas.html) reference

### Windows users — install WSL2 + Ubuntu

The workshop assumes a POSIX shell. The simplest path on Windows is WSL2:

1. Run **PowerShell as Administrator**.
2. `wsl --install -d ubuntu` and press Enter. Restart when prompted.
3. Launch **Ubuntu** from the Start menu and set a username and password.
4. `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y && sudo apt install -y openssh-client git`

Full Microsoft guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install>

### Mac or Linux

Use the built-in **Terminal** app, or install [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/) (Mac) for a nicer experience.

## 2. Create a workshop project

In **RStudio**: *File → New Project → New Directory → New Project*. Name it `scrnaseq_workshop`. Inside that directory create a `data/` folder. The expected layout is:

```
scrnaseq_workshop/
├── scrnaseq_workshop.Rproj
├── data/                    # raw 10x output goes here (Step 4)
└── tutorials/               # downloaded tutorial .qmd files
```

## 3. Install all R / Bioconductor packages

Paste the entire block into your R console. It will take 20–60 minutes the first time.

``` r
# CRAN
cran_pkgs <- c(
  "tidyverse",     # dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, readr, purrr, tibble, stringr, forcats
  "Seurat",        # core scRNA-seq workflow (workshop default)
  "remotes",       # GitHub installs
  "BiocManager",   # Bioconductor installer
  "patchwork",     # combining ggplots
  "presto",        # fast Wilcoxon for FindMarkers
  "harmony",       # batch integration
  "clustree",      # picking clustering resolution
  "ggrepel"        # readable labels on UMAPs
)
install.packages(setdiff(cran_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages())))

# Bioconductor
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
bioc_pkgs <- c(
  "SingleCellExperiment", "scran", "scater", "scuttle",
  "DropletUtils",      # EmptyDrops, knee-point cell calling
  "scDblFinder",       # doublet detection
  "SoupX",             # ambient-RNA correction
  "DESeq2", "edgeR", "limma",
  "fgsea", "clusterProfiler", "ReactomePA", "enrichplot",
  "org.Hs.eg.db", "org.Mm.eg.db",
  "miloR",             # differential abundance
  "SingleR", "celldex",
  "Signac", "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86"
)
BiocManager::install(setdiff(bioc_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages())),
                     update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)

# GitHub / R-universe
remotes::install_github("satijalab/seurat-data", quiet = TRUE, upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("satijalab/azimuth",     quiet = TRUE, upgrade = "never")

# Workshop datasets — these install into your R user library, no manual download
SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")      # ~25 MB; used in Tutorials 01–08
SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")  # ~50 MB; used in Tutorial 11 (Spatial)
```

::: callout-note
The first install will take 20–60 minutes depending on your machine and whether your platform is building from source. **Run it before the workshop, not the morning of.**
:::

## 4. Download the larger workshop dataset (optional)

The core workshop runs on the `ifnb` dataset (installed automatically in Step 3). The **bonus** Talapas Advanced track and the optional NSCLC scaling exercise use the larger 10x 20k NSCLC DTC dataset:

``` bash
# From inside scrnaseq_workshop/
mkdir -p data && cd data

# Filtered feature × barcode matrix (the file the tutorials read)
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz
tar -xzf 20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz
```

You should end up with `data/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/` containing `barcodes.tsv.gz`, `features.tsv.gz`, and `matrix.mtx.gz`.

The scATAC-seq bonus tutorial uses a separate dataset:

``` bash
# Optional: PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1.1 (only for the ATAC bonus tutorial)
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/2.0.0/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.tar.gz
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/2.0.0/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem_fragments.tsv.gz
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/2.0.0/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem/atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
tar -xzf atac_pbmc_10k_nextgem_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.tar.gz
```

See the [Datasets](Datasets.qmd) page for the complete list of datasets and disk-space budget.

## 5. Verify your install

Open a **fresh** R session inside the workshop project and paste:

``` r
pkgs <- c("Seurat","SeuratData","Azimuth",
          "SingleCellExperiment","scran","scater","DropletUtils",
          "scDblFinder","harmony","DESeq2","fgsea","clusterProfiler",
          "miloR","SingleR","celldex","Signac",
          "tidyverse","clustree","presto")
ok <- vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
cat("Package check:\n"); print(ok)
stopifnot(all(ok))

# Load the workshop dataset (auto-installed in Step 3)
SeuratData::LoadData("ifnb")

cat("\nsessionInfo():\n")
sessionInfo()
```

All `TRUE` values and a clean `sessionInfo()` means you're set.

## 6. (Optional) Pin your environment with `renv`

For full reproducibility — and to avoid "it worked yesterday" headaches — pin the exact package versions:

``` r
install.packages("renv")
renv::init()      # one time, in the project root
renv::snapshot()  # writes renv.lock — commit this with your code
```

Anyone who clones the project can `renv::restore()` to recreate the same environment.

## 7. Talapas (UO HPC) — only for the bonus track

Required only if you intend to work through the [Talapas Advanced track](Tutorials.qmd#talapas-advanced-—-hpc-path-raw-fastq-→-differential-abundance) after the workshop.

- Request an account at <https://racs.uoregon.edu/request-access>
- [VS Code & Talapas](Resources_Folder/VSCode_Talapas.html) — account, login, modules, storage
- [Tutorial Talapas 01 — SLURM Basics](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_01_SLURM_Basics.html) — interactive sessions and batch jobs
- [Compute Environments](Compute_Environments.qmd) — Docker/Apptainer image and `renv` lockfile

## Something didn't work?

The [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) documents the issues that come up most often: Mac compiler errors, `BiocManager` mirror selection, RStudio caching old library paths, "permission denied" on Talapas, etc.
